$comment: PLACEHOLDER RECORDS — the company money-in/money-out ledger and its tags. Replaced by GET /admin/finance/transactions and GET /admin/finance/tags. SUPERSEDES spend.json: categories are gone, replaced by tags (see $comment_tags); draft/posted/matched states and recurringRules are gone (see $comment_transactions); salaries are gone entirely (see $comment_tags). Integer paise everywhere.
$comment_tags: Tags are custom: anyone with edit rights creates one, same as any other panel record — the old category list was deliberately closed, this is the reverse of that. What does not change is `kind`, chosen once at creation and never guessed afterwards, because the fixed/reinvestment split behind contribution and CAC is computed from it — changing a tag's kind later rewrites CAC for every month that used it, which is why that edit is rare and audited. Seven tags shipped with the panel (rent, util, soft, ads, vendor, tax, bank); content, travel and supplies were added later by the people who needed them, which is exactly what 'custom' is for. `supplies` is `active: false` — it was deactivated, not deleted, once a single stationery vendor took over what petty cash used to cover ad hoc, and TXN-0914 still points at it: deleting a tag would silently re-bucket every transaction that used it into nothing, so history keeps the tag and the panel renders it as inactive instead. Salaries are not a tag here and never will be — a team member's pay is its own record type in salaries.json, attached to the member record and issued as a numbered slip. Do not create a payroll tag and do not record a salary payment as a company transaction.

$comment_transactions: A row is a fact: it exists because money moved, so there is no draft state and no recurringRules block generating one unattended — every line here was actually paid or actually received on its `valueDate`. `state` is only `recorded` or `cancelled`; nothing is ever edited and nothing is ever deleted. A row that should not stand is CANCELLED with a mandatory reason: every figure on it stays exactly as posted, it stays in the ledger struck through, and it stops counting towards every total. TXN-0917 is the worked example — it was paid to Sharma Carpentry Works when the invoice was Rakesh Contractors', so it carries `state: cancelled`, a `cancellation` block and a TXN_CANCELLED event. Getting the figures right is a NEW row, recorded the ordinary way. Money coming IN is either customer revenue or it is not, and this file only ever carries the second kind: every `direction: 'in'` row here is `nonRevenue: true` with a `creditKind` of `interest`, `own_transfer` or `vendor_refund` (TXN-0902, TXN-0915, TXN-0916). Customer money has exactly one way into the books — a subscription installment payment — and it is never recorded here, faked here, or matched to a bank line here.
